description: We are a multidisciplinary team specialized in data, artificial intelligence, and frontend development. We are creating a space health monitoring software focused on both the individual and the overall mission cohesion. Our solution stands out for using prediction models and AI, interactive 3D visualization, and a local virtual assistant that translates complex medical data into clear alerts and actionable solutions so any astronaut can act immediately.
summary:
UAV (Unity of Astronaut Vitals) is an autonomous, offline-first medical and behavioral monitoring software designed for deep-space missions where communication delays with Earth and the absence of an on-board physician can turn minor health issues or crew friction into mission-ending crises.

UAV addresses this challenge through three pillars:

Collective & Behavioral Intelligence: Cross-referencing individual vitals, cabin environmental sensors, and crew behavioral dynamics to distinguish environmental hazards from contagious outbreaks and prevent interpersonal conflicts.
Personalized Predictive AI: Calibrating locally during the first 14 days of flight to learn each astronaut’s microgravity baseline, predicting fever episodes (48h ahead), mood drops (72h ahead), and burnout with full explainability—zero black boxes.
100% Local Medical RAG + LLM: A clinical assistant grounded in official on-board medical protocols that translates complex alerts into clear, step-by-step instructions for non-medical astronauts without internet access.
details:
UAV — Unity of Astronaut Vitals (by NASAL Operations)

What does it do and how does it work?

UAV (Unity of Astronaut Vitals) is an autonomous, offline-first health and behavioral monitoring system designed for deep-space missions where there is no flight surgeon on board and communication delays with Earth make real-time telemedicine impossible.

Instead of treating astronauts as isolated data streams, UAV monitors the crew as a single interconnected organism across three core pillars:

  1. Collective & Behavioral Health Monitoring: UAV cross-references individual biometric streams with spacecraft cabin sensors (CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​, temperature, radiation, cabin pressure) and crew social dynamics (sleep architecture, social isolation, workload, and interpersonal friction). This allows the system to automatically distinguish between a cabin environmental hazard and a contagious outbreak, while predicting interpersonal or team conflicts before they escalate.
    • Level 1 (Contextual & Deterministic Engine): Evaluates real-time 5-minute wearable streams and daily trends using personalized Z-scores and 7-day rolling windows, generating a continuous Burnout Risk Index (0–100).
    • Level 2 (Predictive Machine Learning): Trained on simulated 60-day mission datasets, our causal ML models anticipate fever episodes 48 hours in advance (AUC-ROC=0.93\text{AUC-ROC} = 0.93AUC-ROC=0.93), mood drops 72 hours in advance, pair/team conflicts 48 hours ahead, and common-cause outbreaks (AUC-ROC=0.99\text{AUC-ROC} = 0.99AUC-ROC=0.99). Every alert includes a strict "Why" explainability block detailing the exact biometric deviations from the astronaut's baseline.
  2. 100% Local Medical RAG + LLM Assistant: When an alert triggers, a non-medical astronaut can open a contextual clinical assistant tied to that specific alert. Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over 25 official on-board clinical protocols and 29 diagnostic rules, a local LLM translates complex telemetry into clear, numbered action steps and escalation criteria (red flags)—with zero hallucinations, zero internet dependency, and strict guardrails preventing the LLM from altering clinical severity.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact?

  • Zero-Latency Autonomous Triage: Empower astronauts with no nursing or medical background to understand and respond to medical and psychological emergencies in seconds, even during communication blackouts on lunar or Martian missions.
  • Proactive Prevention Over Late Reaction: Shifts space medicine from reactive threshold alarms to 48h–72h early intervention, stopping infections, burnout, and crew friction before they compromise the mission.
  • Cognitive Load Reduction: Replaces overwhelming telemetry tables with an intuitive interactive anatomical body map (Heart, Lungs, Brain, Neck, Musculoskeletal, and Cabin Environment) that localizes issues in under 3 seconds.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use?

  • Frontend & Visualization: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js / interactive anatomical UI, and custom mission telemetry dashboards.
  • AI, Machine Learning & Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic, scikit-learn (Calibrated Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Logistic Regression with GroupKFold mission validation), pandas, numpy, and scipy.
  • Local Generative AI & RAG: Local medical RAG indexing clinical protocols (protocols.json & catalogo_alertas.csv) paired with Ollama (qwen2.5:3b / llama3.2:3b) and deterministic clinical fallbacks for guaranteed offline reliability.

How is our project creative & what factors did our team consider?

Our team combines Artificial Intelligence, Multimedia Design, and Criminology. Bringing a criminology and behavioral analysis perspective into space medicine allowed us to model human confinement dynamics, social isolation, and partner friction alongside vital signs. We specifically engineered UAV around real spaceflight constraints: physiological adaptation to microgravity (14-day personalized calibration), strict offline operation, clinical safety (prohibiting black-box alerts or AI severity overrides), and high-stress usability for non-medical crew members.
